---
title: "Eastern Bering Sea Walleye Pollock Early Survival Pathways"
description: "A Quarto synthesis of causal hypotheses and DAG alternatives for prerecruit survival to age 3."
---

This site summarizes causal hypotheses for eastern Bering Sea walleye pollock survival from eggs and larvae through age-0, age-1, and age-2 fish reaching age 3. The synthesis is based on the local paper set in the parent reprints folder, with web-visible citation links supplied through DOI and source URLs.

The papers often quantify recruitment at age 1 or age 2. Here, **age-3 recruitment** means the same cohort passing through the prerecruit filters and remaining alive and available at age 3.

## Main Conclusion

Two mechanisms have the clearest support:

1. **Age-0 energy gate.** Late-summer and fall condition, especially total energy, lipid reserves, and access to lipid-rich copepods and euphausiids, strongly affects overwinter survival to age 1 [@heintz2013; @siddon2013; @sogard2000; @sigler2016].
2. **Age-1 predation gate.** Juvenile survival after the first winter is strongly affected by spatial overlap with adult pollock, arrowtooth flounder, and other predators, with age-1 mortality particularly important [@mueter2006; @spencer2016].

Temperature, sea ice, stratification, summer wind mixing, and transport matter because they modify these gates. Average temperature alone is a useful proxy only when the active pathway is unresolved [@smart2012; @petrik2015; @gann2016].

## Practical Model

The minimum useful causal model is:

```text
Age3_recruitment =
  f(spawner output,
    age0 energy condition,
    age1-age2 predator overlap,
    cohort density,
    observation/assessment uncertainty)
```

In that model, age-0 condition is a mediator of ice timing, bloom timing, summer mixing, prey production, and SST. Predator overlap is a mediator of cold pool area, predator biomass, juvenile distribution, and adult pollock biomass.
